title: CancellationToken in consumers
hook: CancellationToken is a cooperative flag plus callbacks. SQS and RabbitMQ shutdown only works if every await observes the same token the host cancelled.

sections.heading: Cooperative, not preemptive
sections.prose: CancellationToken is a struct view over a CancellationTokenSource. Cancel sets IsCancellationRequested and runs registered callbacks. It does not abort a thread. HttpClient, StackExchange.Redis, and AWS SDK calls that take a token will complete early or throw OperationCanceledException. A tight CPU loop must call ThrowIfCancellationRequested itself. For a RabbitMQ or SQS consumer, the generic host’s StoppingToken is the process lifetime. Pass it into the receive loop. When Kubernetes sends SIGTERM, you stop fetching, finish or nack the in-flight message according to policy, then exit before the grace period. Do not create a token source per message and forget to dispose it; use `await using` on linked sources.

snippets.label: SQS loop with host token and per-message timeout
snippets.explanation: Linked tokens expire a hung receive without treating host shutdown and a 25-second timeout as the same condition.

sections.heading: What to ack when cancelled
sections.prose: If stoppingToken fires mid-handle, decide explicitly. Requeue (SQS: skip DeleteMessage, let visibility timeout expire; RabbitMQ: nack requeue true) when the work is idempotent. Drop or send to a DLQ when a partial side effect already committed. Never ignore the token in a Redis SET that is part of the same unit of work you will retry. Register callbacks for non-async resources (a raw socket abort) with token.Register, and dispose the registration. Passing CancellationToken.None in a public library method is a smell unless the operation truly cannot stop.

interviewTakeaways: Cancellation is cooperative: unused tokens do nothing.
Link host lifetime tokens with per-operation timeouts.
Distinguish shutdown cancellation from timeout when deciding ack versus nack.
commonPitfalls: Catching Exception and nacking cancellation as a poison message during deploy.
Forgetting to pass the token into nested Redis and HTTP calls.
Leaking CancellationTokenSource instances in a 999-message/second loop.

jsTsCorrelations.note: AbortSignal is the JS cousin: fetch observes it, CPU loops must poll aborted. C# tokens also multicast to many operations through linked sources.
